name: Error Handling Patterns
description: Error handling — custom error classes, error boundaries, graceful degradation, structured logging, recovery
content:
# Error Handling Patterns

- Define custom error classes with error codes, status codes, and user-friendly messages — distinguish between operational errors and programmer errors
- Use error boundaries (React `ErrorBoundary`, framework equivalents) to catch rendering errors and display fallback UI instead of a white screen
- Design for graceful degradation — when a non-critical service fails, disable that feature rather than crashing the entire application
- Use structured logging (JSON format) with consistent fields: timestamp, level, error code, message, stack trace, and request context
- Implement retry logic with exponential backoff for transient failures (network timeouts, rate limits, temporary service outages)
- Never swallow errors silently — every `catch` block should log, report, re-throw, or handle the error explicitly
- Return meaningful error responses to API consumers — include error codes, human-readable messages, and documentation links when relevant
- Separate error handling from business logic — use middleware, interceptors, or centralized error handlers rather than try-catch in every function
- Monitor error rates and set up alerts — track error frequency, new error types, and error spikes to catch issues before users report them
- Test error paths explicitly — write tests for network failures, invalid input, missing permissions, and timeout scenarios, not just the happy path
